0.content: Kaveh, the celebrated Kshahrewar architect, is two years older than Alhaitham and was once his closest friend. They met in the library as students and ran one joint project on King Deshret's ruins that brought real academic results. They fell out over whether talent or effort should decide who belongs in research, Kaveh's guilt-driven altruism, and Alhaitham's egoism. Alhaitham removed his name from the thesis; Kaveh tore up his copy, then taped it back together. Years later Alhaitham found him penniless at Lambad's Tavern after Kaveh's commission for the Palace of Alcazarzaray bankrupted him, and took him in.

key: Decoding the Runes and Architectural Philosophy
1.comment: Alhaitham: Alhaitham's Home and the joint thesis
1.content: The house near the Akademiya began as a research site the Akademiya assigned to Alhaitham and Kaveh's joint project. When the project stalled for lack of manpower and a shared vision, its assets passed to the researchers. The Akademiya later used the forgotten project to allocate housing, so Alhaitham got a very decent home. Kaveh, through an intermediary, declined his half.

2.content: Alhaitham neither dismisses nor reveres gods; he thinks gods need followers and are part of a hierarchy like any other being. He takes no pride in having helped rescue one, and hopes Nahida won't take offence. She sometimes invites him to the Sanctuary of Surasthana to discuss matters. She credits him with a mind so advanced nothing could fool him, but questions whether the wise should see the mediocre majority as defective, "because without them, there is no us."

3.comment: Alhaitham: The Divine Knowledge Capsule and Port Ormos
3.content: The Traveler first met Alhaitham at Port Ormos, quarrelling with the radical Eremite band Ayn Al-Ahmar, whose leader Mizri had acquired an Akademiya item: a Divine Knowledge Capsule. Alhaitham wanted to study what "divine knowledge" really was. He paid the Traveler to become customers of the merchant Dori, who would not deal with Akademiya people, and tested ordinary Canned Knowledge in the wild. At the arranged fight Mizri used the Capsule and went berserk. Alhaitham ended it by cutting Mizri's connection to his Akasha Terminal.

4.content: Cyno, the General Mahamatra, ambushed the group at Aaru Village demanding the Capsule. He and Alhaitham clashed to a standstill and were still ready to fight when Dehya stepped in. Cyno had exiled himself after finding falsified data from Azar. Later Alhaitham told him the sages had used the Akasha's computation to predict Cyno's every movement. If the culprits always went where Cyno wasn't, they must be in the desert.

5.content: Dehya, a mercenary of the Eremites, joined the plot against the sages, risked her arm to win Rahman's trust in her friends, and led the diversion on Jnagarbha Day. Alhaitham offered her a post at the Akademiya. She refused: it would bore her to death. She mocks his long sentences and snooty tone. He sighs that a predictable life isn't her cup of tea.

6.content: Nilou's dance at the Akademiya gate was part of Alhaitham's Jnagarbha Day plan; as guards dragged him out after his staged outburst, he exchanged a glance with her. Later she asked how he had survived the Divine Knowledge Capsule. He deflected by asking why Cyno and Dehya, just as curious, had been too shy to ask. He thinks she knows her strengths and lives a happy, simple life.

7.comment: Alhaitham: Jnagarbha Day and the fall of the sages
7.content: Alhaitham planned the operation to free Lesser Lord Kusanali. On Jnagarbha Day he walked the Traveler straight in the Akademiya's front door. Caught by Grand Sage Azar, he appeared to betray the Traveler, then flew into an apparent fit of madness, lunging at Azar and knocking over a rack of Knowledge Capsules. Azar ordered him exiled to Aaru Village and locked the Traveler in exactly the room from which they could reach Nahida's consciousness. As he was dragged out, his terminal's light returned to normal green.

8.comment: Alhaitham: Acting Grand Sage and Siraj's hivemind
8.content: After the coup he refused the Grand Sage's seat and reluctantly served as Acting Grand Sage, while rumours about him spread through the Akademiya. In his Story Quest he investigated the scholar Ilyas, who said a Vahumana scholar, Siraj, had abducted him. Siraj, Alhaitham's former classmate, had built a hivemind of ranked scholars ("Siraj #36"). Earlier, Alhaitham had rejected Siraj's paper because it touched human evolution, one of the Akademiya's cardinal sins.

9.content: He and the Traveler began as wary partners who hid things from each other, and ended as the two key pieces of the plan to free Nahida. He thinks the Traveler is perfectly able to look after themselves and even look after Paimon, and has no advice to offer. He does not coddle Paimon: before Jnagarbha Day he left the encouragement to Candace.

key: may my child Alhaitham lead a peaceful life
10.content: His father, a Haravatat mentor, and his mother, a renowned Vahumana scholar, died in an accident when he was very small. His grandmother, a Kshahrewar scholar, raised him and recognised his parents' talent and temperament in him. When he rejected school after half a day, she let him teach himself from her paper books. Her parting advice: clever people tend to large egos and acting alone, so he must keep a clearer mind than others and recognise vain pursuits as dust.
